questions.title: Question 1: Information Processing Style
questions.text: When you encounter new information, you prefer to:

options.A: Read detailed explanations and research multiple sources thoroughly
options.B: Jump in and learn by doing, experimenting hands-on immediately
options.C: Discuss it with others and learn through conversation and collaboration
options.D: See examples and practice with guided, step-by-step instruction

questions.title: Question 2: Ideal Study Environment
questions.text: Your most productive study environment is:

options.A: A quiet library with access to many books and research materials
options.B: A lab or workspace where you can build, create, and experiment
options.C: A collaborative space where you can work and discuss with others
options.D: A comfortable, organized personal space with minimal distractions

questions.title: Question 3: Problem-Solving Approach
questions.text: When solving problems, you typically:

options.A: Research thoroughly and gather all available information first
options.B: Try different approaches through trial and error until something works
options.C: Talk through the problem with others to gain different perspectives
options.D: Follow a systematic, methodical step-by-step approach

questions.title: Question 4: Memory and Retention
questions.text: You remember information best when:

options.A: You write detailed notes and review them regularly over time
options.B: You act it out, create something with it, or use it practically
options.C: You explain it to someone else or discuss it in groups
options.D: You practice it repeatedly in different contexts and situations

questions.title: Question 5: Learning Challenges
questions.text: When learning gets difficult, you prefer to:

options.A: Find additional resources, books, and supplementary materials
options.B: Break it down into smaller parts and tackle each piece practically
options.C: Form a study group or find a study partner for support
options.D: Seek direct help and guidance from a teacher or tutor

questions.title: Question 6: Information Format Preference
questions.text: You learn most effectively from:

options.A: Written materials like textbooks, articles, and detailed handouts
options.B: Interactive demonstrations, videos, and hands-on activities
options.C: Lectures, discussions, podcasts, and verbal explanations
options.D: Visual aids like charts, diagrams, mind maps, and infographics

questions.title: Question 7: Study Session Structure
questions.text: Your ideal study session involves:

options.A: Extended periods of focused reading and note-taking
options.B: Short bursts of active practice with frequent breaks
options.C: Group study sessions with discussion and collaboration
options.D: Structured time blocks with clear goals and checkpoints

questions.title: Question 8: Feedback Preference
questions.text: You prefer to receive feedback that is:

options.A: Detailed written comments with specific suggestions for improvement
options.B: Immediate and practical, showing you what to do differently
options.C: Given verbally through conversation and discussion
options.D: Visual and measurable, showing your progress over time

questions.title: Question 9: Learning Motivation
questions.text: You feel most motivated to learn when:

options.A: The material connects to your academic goals and interests
options.B: You can see real-world applications and practical uses
options.C: You're learning alongside others who share your interests
options.D: You have clear milestones and can track your progress

questions.title: Question 10: Attention and Focus
questions.text: You maintain focus best when:

options.A: Working in complete silence with minimal interruptions
options.B: Having some background activity or music while working
options.C: Surrounded by the energy of other people working
options.D: In a comfortable environment that you can control and adjust

questions.title: Question 11: Learning Pace
questions.text: Your natural learning pace is:

options.A: Slow and thorough, taking time to fully understand each concept
options.B: Fast and energetic, covering lots of material quickly
options.C: Conversational, learning through back-and-forth discussion
options.D: Balanced, alternating between different speeds as needed

questions.title: Question 12: Knowledge Application
questions.text: You feel you truly understand something when:

options.A: You can explain all the theory and background concepts
options.B: You can use it to solve real problems or create something
options.C: You can teach it to someone else successfully
options.D: You can connect it to other things you already know

questions.title: Question 13: Note-Taking Style
questions.text: Your preferred note-taking method is:

options.A: Detailed written notes with complete sentences and paragraphs
options.B: Quick sketches, diagrams, and bullet points with key concepts
options.C: Recording discussions or summarizing what others have said
options.D: Organized outlines with clear headings and structured format

questions.title: Question 14: Test Preparation
questions.text: When preparing for exams, you typically:

options.A: Create comprehensive study guides and review all materials multiple times
options.B: Focus on practice problems and hands-on application of concepts
options.C: Form study groups and quiz each other on the material
options.D: Use flashcards, timelines, and visual organizers to structure information

questions.title: Question 15: New Concept Introduction
questions.text: When a teacher introduces a new concept, you prefer they:

options.A: Provide extensive background reading and theoretical foundation
options.B: Start with a demonstration or real-world example
options.C: Begin with a class discussion about what students already know
options.D: Present a clear outline of what will be covered and why

questions.title: Question 16: Assignment Preferences
questions.text: You perform best on assignments that:

options.A: Require extensive research and written analysis
options.B: Involve building, creating, or experimenting with materials
options.C: Include group work or peer collaboration components
options.D: Have clear rubrics and step-by-step requirements

questions.title: Question 17: Learning from Mistakes
questions.text: When you make a mistake, you prefer to:

options.A: Research what went wrong and understand the underlying principles
options.B: Try again immediately with a different approach
options.C: Discuss the mistake with others to get their insights
options.D: Review the correct process step-by-step before trying again

questions.title: Question 18: Technology in Learning
questions.text: You find technology most helpful when it:

options.A: Provides access to extensive databases and research materials
options.B: Offers interactive simulations and hands-on digital tools
options.C: Enables collaboration and communication with other learners
options.D: Organizes information clearly and tracks your learning progress

questions.title: Question 19: Long-term Retention
questions.text: You best retain information over time when you:

options.A: Regularly review and re-read your notes and materials
options.B: Continue to use and apply the knowledge in practical situations
options.C: Regularly discuss and share the information with others
options.D: Create visual reminders and review them systematically

questions.title: Question 20: Learning Satisfaction
questions.text: You feel most satisfied with your learning when:

options.A: You have thoroughly mastered the theoretical foundations
options.B: You can successfully apply knowledge to solve real problems
options.C: You can engage in meaningful discussions about the topic
options.D: You can see clear evidence of your progress and achievement

A.name: Scholarly Learner (Theoretical/Reading-focused)
A.summary: You learn best through deep reading, research, and careful analysis. Quiet study spaces, detailed notes, and comprehensive understanding are your strengths.
scoring_bullets: Thrives with written materials and quiet study
Values thorough understanding and academic rigor
Learns best through comprehensive analysis and reflection

B.name: Experiential Learner (Kinesthetic/Hands-on)
B.summary: You learn best by doing. Hands-on activities, real-world applications, and experimentation help you understand and remember information.
scoring_bullets: Learns best through hands-on experience and experimentation
Prefers active, practical applications over theory
Motivated by real-world connections and immediate application
Thrives in dynamic, interactive learning environments

C.name: Social Learner (Auditory/Collaborative)
C.summary: You learn best through discussion, collaboration, and verbal processing. Study groups, conversations, and teaching others help ideas stick.
scoring_bullets: Learns through discussion, collaboration, and verbal processing
Values different perspectives and group interactions
Motivated by interpersonal connections and shared learning
Processes information best through talking and listening

D.name: Structured Learner (Visual/Organized)
D.summary: You learn best with clear structure, visual organization, and step-by-step guidance. Plans, checklists, and visual tools support your success.
scoring_bullets: Prefers organized, systematic approaches to learning
Values clear guidance, visual aids, and measurable progress
Thrives with balanced, methodical learning processes
Learns best with clear structure and visual organization

scoring_intro: Scoring Guide: Count your responses for each letter:
mixed_results: Mixed Results: Many learners have a combination of preferences. Look at your top two categories to understand your primary and secondary learning styles.
